fixed_before: holdout sentence selection, annotation, and any holdout prediction

data.selection: CELL pilot procedure (src/cell_pilot.py) applied to holdout students: structural metadata for students, parser-derived structural categories for sentences; no labels, verdicts, predictions, quality, length, or duplicate flags

parse.pipeline: frozen en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 with spaCy 3.8.13 (sentence segmentation v1)
parse.context: each sentence is a span of its complete essay parse

annotation.labeller: a separate model session (annotator_id claude_sealed_holdout_v1) that sees only a blind packet: sentence, neighbouring sentences, token parse, clause heads, and the annotation guideline
labeller_must_not_see: Syntax Reliability verdicts or flags of any version
Reliability ML features, probabilities, or predictions
development results, error analyses, and project history
annotation.owner_review: the dataset owner reviews every UNRELIABLE, MOSTLY_RELIABLE, and NOT_ANALYZABLE label and a seeded random sample of 40 RELIABLE labels (seed 20261105); reviewed records become adjudicated by human_owner_v1
annotation.freeze: labels are locked by file hash before the evaluation run; no label changes after the run

systems.reference: Syntax Reliability v1.2 warning (medium or low)
systems.primary_candidate: Syntax Reliability v1.3 warning (medium or low)
systems.secondary_candidate: Reliability ML Model B (feature schema 1.0 with v1.2 signals, balanced logistic regression as in ML v1) refit on all 606 development observations, with one threshold chosen by the heuristic_precision rule on the 5-fold student-grouped out-of-fold probabilities of the development set
not_evaluated: Model A and Model C, which did not beat Model B on development data
Clause Detection v2.2 and sentence segmentation v2, whose labels would need re-judging

analysis.analysis_set: labelled analyzable sentences where v1.2 does not abstain; abstentions are counted and reported separately
metrics: true and false positive and negative counts
analysis.paired_comparison: v1.3 against v1.2 and Model B against v1.2: discordant counts on UNRELIABLE sentences (recall) and on usable sentences (false warnings), each with a two-sided exact McNemar test
analysis.primary_question: Does v1.3 raise recall over v1.2 without lowering precision?
analysis.decision_rule: v1.3 becomes the reference heuristic if its recall gain on UNRELIABLE sentences is significant (exact McNemar p < 0.05) and it adds no significant false warnings; otherwise the result is reported as inconclusive or negative and v1.3 stays a development candidate
analysis.power_note: the v1.3 patterns occurred in 9 of 420 pilot sentences, so few discordant pairs are expected and an inconclusive result is likely

opening_procedure: freeze this plan, the evaluated code, and the development set lock in git
complete annotation and owner review, then lock the holdout labels by hash
record the opening date and reason in split_v1.json (holdout_opened_at, holdout_open_reason) and in PROJECT_HISTORY.md
run the evaluation once and report every planned number, whatever the outcome
after opening, the 25 evaluated students are no longer untouched; later claims of untouched evaluation must use other holdout students
